title_en: Law on Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted in accordance with the Constitution for the purposes of preventing, controlling and eliminating occupational disease hazards, preventing and treating occupational diseases, protecting the health and related rights and interests of workers, and promoting economic and social development.

Article 2 This Law shall apply to the activities of prevention and treatment of occupational diseases within the territory of the People's Republic of China.
For the purposes of this Law, "occupational diseases" means diseases caused by exposure to dust, radioactive substances and other toxic and harmful factors in occupational activities by workers of employing units such as enterprises, public institutions and individual economic organizations.
The classification and catalogue of occupational diseases shall be formulated, adjusted and published by the health administration department of the State Council jointly with the labor and social security administration department of the State Council.

Article 3 The work of prevention and treatment of occupational diseases shall adhere to the principle of giving priority to prevention and combining prevention with treatment, establish a mechanism under which the employing units are responsible, administrative organs supervise, industry self-regulates, workers participate and the public supervises, and implement classified management and comprehensive treatment.

Article 4 Workers shall enjoy the right to occupational health protection according to law.
Employing units shall create working environments and conditions that meet the national occupational health standards and health requirements, and take measures to ensure that workers receive occupational health protection.
Trade union organizations shall supervise the work of prevention and treatment of occupational diseases according to law and safeguard the lawful rights and interests of workers. When formulating or amending rules and regulations concerning the prevention and treatment of occupational diseases, the employing unit shall solicit the opinions of the trade union organization.

Article 5 Employing units shall establish and improve the responsibility system for the prevention and treatment of occupational diseases, strengthen the management of such prevention and treatment, raise the level of such prevention and treatment, and bear responsibility for the occupational disease hazards arising from their units.
Article 6 The principal person in charge of an employing unit shall take full responsibility for the work of prevention and treatment of occupational diseases in the unit.

Article 7 Employing units must participate in work-related injury insurance according to law.
The labor and social security administration departments of the State Council and of the local people's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen the supervision and management of work-related injury insurance to ensure that workers enjoy work-related injury insurance benefits according to law.

Article 8 The State shall encourage and support the research, development, promotion and application of new technologies, new techniques, new equipment and new materials that are conducive to the prevention and treatment of occupational diseases and the protection of workers' health, strengthen basic research on the mechanisms and occurrence patterns of occupational diseases, and raise the scientific and technological level of prevention and treatment of occupational diseases; it shall actively adopt effective technologies, techniques, equipment and materials for prevention and treatment of occupational diseases; and it shall restrict the use or eliminate technologies, techniques, equipment and materials that cause serious occupational disease hazards.
The State shall encourage and support the construction of medical and rehabilitation institutions for occupational diseases.

Article 9 The State shall implement a system of occupational health supervision.
The health administration department and the labor and social security administration department of the State Council shall, in accordance with this Law and the functions and duties determined by the State Council, be responsible for the supervision and management of the prevention and treatment of occupational diseases nationwide. The relevant departments of the State Council shall be responsible for the relevant supervision and management of the prevention and treatment of occupational diseases within their respective functions and duties.
The health administration departments and the labor and social security administration departments of the local people's governments at or above the county level shall, based on their respective functions and duties, be responsible for the supervision and management of the prevention and treatment of occupational diseases within their respective administrative regions. The relevant departments of the local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for the relevant supervision and management of the prevention and treatment of occupational diseases within their respective functions and duties.
The health administration departments and the labor and social security administration departments of the people's governments at or above the county level (hereinafter collectively referred to as the "occupational health supervision and administration departments") shall strengthen communication, closely cooperate, exercise their powers and assume responsibilities according to law in line with their respective division of functions and duties.

Article 10 The State Council and the local people's governments at or above the county level shall formulate plans for the prevention and treatment of occupational diseases, incorporate them into the national economic and social development plans, and organize their implementation.
The local people's governments at or above the county level shall be uniformly responsible for, lead, organize and coordinate the work of prevention and treatment of occupational diseases within their respective administrative regions, establish and improve the working system and mechanism for such prevention and treatment, and uniformly lead and command the response to occupational health emergencies; they shall strengthen the capacity building and service system construction for prevention and treatment of occupational diseases, and perfect and implement the responsibility system for such work.
The people's governments of townships, nationality townships, and towns shall earnestly implement this Law and support the occupational health supervision and administration departments in performing their duties according to law.

Article 11 The occupational health supervision and administration departments of the people's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen the publicity and education on the prevention and treatment of occupational diseases, disseminate knowledge thereof, enhance the awareness of employing units regarding such prevention and treatment, and raise workers' occupational health awareness, self-protection awareness and ability to exercise their rights to occupational health protection.

Article 12 The national occupational health standards concerning the prevention and treatment of occupational diseases shall be organized for formulation and published by the health administration department of the State Council.
The health administration department of the State Council shall organize and carry out monitoring of key occupational diseases and special investigations, assess occupational health risks, and provide scientific basis for formulating occupational health standards and policies for the prevention and treatment of occupational diseases.
The health administration departments of the local people's governments at or above the county level shall regularly conduct statistics and survey analysis on the situation of prevention and treatment of occupational diseases within their respective administrative regions.

Article 13 Any unit or individual shall have the right to report and accuse any act violating this Law. The relevant departments, upon receiving such reports and accusations, shall handle them in a timely manner.
Units and individuals that have achieved outstanding success in the prevention and treatment of occupational diseases shall be given rewards.

Article 14 Employing units shall, in accordance with the requirements of laws and regulations, strictly abide by the national occupational health standards, implement occupational disease prevention measures, and control and eliminate occupational disease hazards at the source.

Article 16 The State shall establish a system for reporting projects involving occupational disease hazards.
Where the workplaces of an employing unit contain occupational disease hazard factors listed in the catalogue of occupational diseases, the employing unit shall promptly and truthfully report the hazardous projects to the local health administration department and accept supervision.
The classified catalogue of occupational disease hazard factors shall be formulated, adjusted and published by the health administration department of the State Council. The specific measures for reporting projects involving occupational disease hazards shall be formulated by the health administration department of the State Council.

Article 17 For a construction project of new construction, expansion, or reconstruction, or a project for technological transformation or technology introduction (hereinafter collectively referred to as "construction projects") which may produce occupational disease hazards, the construction entity shall conduct a pre-assessment of occupational disease hazards at the feasibility study stage.
For a construction project of a medical institution which may produce radioactive occupational disease hazards, the construction entity shall submit a pre-assessment report on radioactive occupational disease hazards to the health administration department. The health administration department shall, within thirty days of receiving the pre-assessment report, make a review decision and notify the construction entity in writing. Where no pre-assessment report is submitted, or the pre-assessment report is not approved by the health administration department upon review, construction shall not commence.
The pre-assessment report on occupational disease hazards shall assess the occupational disease hazard factors that may be produced by the construction project and their impact on the workplace and workers' health, and determine the hazard category and the protective measures against occupational diseases.
The measures for classified management of occupational disease hazards in construction projects shall be formulated by the health administration department of the State Council.

Article 18 The cost of occupational disease protection facilities for a construction project shall be included in the project budget, and shall be designed, constructed, and put into production and use simultaneously with the main project.
The design of occupational disease protection facilities for a construction project shall comply with the national occupational health standards and health requirements; for construction projects of medical institutions with serious radioactive occupational disease hazards, construction of the protection facilities shall not proceed until the design has been examined and approved by the health administration department.
Before the completion and acceptance of a construction project, the construction entity shall conduct an assessment of the effectiveness of occupational disease hazard control.
For the construction project of a medical institution which may produce radioactive occupational disease hazards, the radioactive occupational disease protection facilities may only be put into use after they have passed the acceptance inspection by the health administration department; the occupational disease protection facilities of other construction projects shall be organized for acceptance inspection by the construction entity according to law, and may only be put into production and use after passing the acceptance inspection. The health administration department shall strengthen the supervision and inspection of the acceptance activities organized by the construction entity and the results thereof.

Article 19 The State shall implement special management for operations involving radioactive substances, highly toxic substances, high-risk dust, and the like. The specific management measures shall be formulated by the State Council.

Article 21 Employing units shall ensure the funding necessary for the prevention and treatment of occupational diseases, shall not divert or misappropriate such funds, and shall bear responsibility for the consequences arising from insufficient funding.

Article 22 Employing units must adopt effective occupational disease protection facilities and provide workers with personal protective equipment for occupational diseases.
The personal protective equipment for occupational diseases provided by employing units to workers must meet the requirements for the prevention and treatment of occupational diseases; equipment that does not meet the requirements shall not be used.

Article 23 Employing units shall give priority to the adoption of new technologies, new techniques, new equipment and new materials that are conducive to the prevention and treatment of occupational diseases and the protection of workers' health, and gradually replace technologies, techniques, equipment and materials that cause serious occupational disease hazards.

Article 24 An employing unit that produces occupational disease hazards shall set up a bulletin board in a prominent position to publish the relevant rules and regulations on prevention and treatment of occupational diseases, operating procedures, emergency rescue measures for occupational disease hazard accidents, and the test results of occupational disease hazard factors in the workplace.
For work posts that produce serious occupational disease hazards, warning signs and Chinese warning instructions shall be placed in prominent positions. The warning instructions shall specify the types of occupational disease hazards produced, their consequences, prevention measures, and emergency treatment measures, among other things.

Article 25 For toxic and harmful workplaces where acute occupational injuries may occur, the employing unit shall install alarm devices, provide onsite first-aid supplies, flushing equipment, emergency evacuation passages and necessary decontamination areas.
For radiation workplaces and the transport and storage of radioactive isotopes, the employing unit must be equipped with protective equipment and alarm devices, and ensure that workers exposed to radiation wear personal dosimeters.
Employing units shall conduct regular maintenance and repair of occupational disease protection equipment, emergency rescue facilities, and personal protective equipment for occupational diseases, periodically test their performance and effectiveness, and ensure that they are in normal condition; such equipment and facilities shall not be dismantled or stopped from use without authorization.

Article 26 Employing units shall implement daily monitoring of occupational disease hazard factors by designated personnel, and ensure that the monitoring system is in normal operation.
Employing units shall, in accordance with the regulations of the health administration department of the State Council, regularly conduct testing and assessment of occupational disease hazard factors in the workplace. The results of such testing and assessment shall be kept in the occupational health archives of the employing unit, periodically reported to the local health administration department, and published to workers.
The testing and assessment of occupational disease hazard factors shall be conducted by occupational health technical service institutions established according to law, which have obtained qualification recognition from the health administration department of the State Council or from the health administration departments of the local people's governments at or above the city with districts in accordance with the division of functions and duties. The testing and assessment conducted by occupational health technical service institutions shall be objective and truthful.
Where it is found that occupational disease hazard factors in the workplace do not comply with the national occupational health standards and health requirements, the employing unit shall immediately take corresponding control measures; if the standards and requirements still cannot be met, the operation involving such hazard factors must be stopped; the operation may resume only after the hazard factors have been controlled and comply with the national occupational health standards and health requirements.

Article 27 Occupational health technical service institutions shall engage in the testing and assessment of occupational disease hazard factors according to law and shall accept supervision and inspection by the health administration departments. The health administration departments shall perform their supervisory duties according to law.

Article 28 Anyone who provides equipment that may produce occupational disease hazards to an employing unit shall provide a Chinese instruction manual, and place a warning sign and Chinese warning instructions in a prominent position on the equipment. The warning instructions shall specify the performance of the equipment, the occupational disease hazards that may be produced, safety operation and maintenance precautions, occupational disease protection measures, and emergency treatment measures, among other things.

Article 29 Anyone who provides to an employing unit chemicals, radioactive isotopes, or materials containing radioactive substances that may produce occupational disease hazards shall provide a Chinese instruction manual. The instruction manual shall specify the characteristics of the product, main ingredients, harmful factors present, possible harmful consequences, safety precautions for use, occupational disease protection measures, and emergency treatment measures, among other things. The product packaging shall bear conspicuous warning signs and Chinese warning instructions. Premises where the aforesaid materials are stored shall have danger signs or radioactive warning signs placed in the prescribed locations.
For chemical materials related to occupational disease hazards that are used or imported for the first time in China, the user or importer shall, after obtaining approval from the relevant department of the State Council in accordance with state regulations, submit to the health administration department of the State Council the toxicity assessment of such chemical materials and the documents of registration or import approval from the relevant department.
The import of radioactive isotopes, radiation devices and articles containing radioactive substances shall be handled in accordance with the relevant state provisions.
Article 30 No unit or individual may produce, operate, import or use equipment or materials that are explicitly prohibited by the State and may produce occupational disease hazards.

Article 31 No unit or individual may transfer operations that produce occupational disease hazards to units or individuals that do not have the conditions for occupational disease protection. Units or individuals that do not have the conditions for occupational disease protection shall not accept operations that produce occupational disease hazards.

Article 32 An employing unit shall be aware of the occupational disease hazards produced by the technologies, techniques, equipment and materials it adopts; if it adopts technologies, techniques, equipment or materials that have occupational disease hazards while concealing such hazards, it shall bear responsibility for the consequences of the occupational disease hazards caused.

Article 33 When concluding a labor contract (including an employment contract, the same below) with a worker, the employing unit shall truthfully inform the worker of the occupational disease hazards that may arise during the work process, their consequences, protective measures against occupational diseases, and benefits, and shall specify these in the labor contract; it shall not conceal or deceive.
Where, during the term of an existing labor contract, a worker is assigned to perform operations involving occupational disease hazards that were not disclosed in the labor contract due to changes in job position or work content, the employing unit shall, in accordance with the preceding paragraph, perform the obligation of truthful disclosure to the worker and negotiate modifications to the relevant terms of the original labor contract.
If an employing unit violates the provisions of the preceding two paragraphs, the worker shall have the right to refuse to perform the operations involving occupational disease hazards, and the employing unit shall not terminate the labor contract concluded with the worker on this ground.

Article 34 The principal person in charge and the occupational health management personnel of an employing unit shall receive occupational health training, comply with the laws and regulations on prevention and treatment of occupational diseases, and organize the unit's work of prevention and treatment of occupational diseases according to law.
Employing units shall provide workers with pre-job occupational health training and regular on-the-job occupational health training, disseminate occupational health knowledge, urge workers to comply with the laws, regulations, rules and operating procedures on prevention and treatment of occupational diseases, and instruct workers in the correct use of occupational disease protection equipment and personal protective equipment for occupational diseases.
Workers shall study and master relevant occupational health knowledge, enhance their awareness of occupational disease prevention, comply with the laws, regulations, rules and operating procedures on prevention and treatment of occupational diseases, correctly use and maintain occupational disease protection equipment and personal protective equipment for occupational diseases, and promptly report any hidden dangers of occupational disease hazard accidents.
If a worker fails to perform the obligations specified in the preceding paragraph, the employing unit shall provide education to the worker.

Article 35 For workers engaged in operations involving exposure to occupational disease hazards, the employing unit shall, in accordance with the regulations of the health administration department of the State Council, organize occupational health examinations before employment, during employment, and at the time of leaving the job, and shall inform the workers of the examination results in writing. The costs of occupational health examinations shall be borne by the employing unit.
Employing units shall not assign workers who have not undergone pre-employment occupational health examinations to operations involving exposure to occupational disease hazards; they shall not assign workers with occupational contraindications to the operations they are contraindicated from; workers found during occupational health examinations to have health damage related to the occupation they are engaged in shall be transferred from their original posts and properly placed; and workers who have not undergone an occupational health examination before leaving their jobs shall not have their labor contracts dissolved or terminated.
Occupational health examinations shall be conducted by medical and health institutions that have obtained a "Practicing License for Medical Institutions". The health administration department shall strengthen the standardized management of occupational health examination work, and the specific management measures shall be formulated by the health administration department of the State Council.

Article 36 Employing units shall establish occupational health surveillance files for workers and keep them properly for the prescribed period.
Occupational health surveillance files shall include workers' occupational history, history of exposure to occupational disease hazards, results of occupational health examinations, and diagnosis and treatment of occupational diseases, among other personal health data.
When a worker leaves the employing unit, the worker shall have the right to obtain a copy of his or her own occupational health surveillance file, and the employing unit shall provide it truthfully and free of charge, and shall affix its seal on the copy provided.

Article 37 When an acute occupational disease hazard accident occurs or is likely to occur, the employing unit shall immediately take emergency rescue and control measures, and promptly report to the local health administration department and relevant departments. Upon receiving the report, the health administration department shall promptly organize investigation and handling together with the relevant departments; if necessary, it may take temporary control measures. The health administration department shall organize and ensure proper medical treatment.
For workers who have suffered or may suffer from acute occupational disease hazards, the employing unit shall promptly organize treatment, conduct health examinations and medical observation, and the necessary costs shall be borne by the employing unit.

Article 38 Employing units shall not assign minor workers to operations involving exposure to occupational disease hazards; they shall not assign female workers during pregnancy or lactation to operations that are harmful to themselves, their fetuses or infants.

Article 40 Trade union organizations shall urge and assist employing units in carrying out occupational health publicity, education and training, and shall have the right to put forward opinions and suggestions on the prevention and treatment of occupational diseases by employing units, sign special collective contracts on labor safety and health with employing units on behalf of workers according to law, and coordinate with employing units on issues concerning the prevention and treatment of occupational diseases raised by workers and urge their resolution.
Trade union organizations shall have the right to demand that employing units correct any act that violates laws and regulations on the prevention and treatment of occupational diseases and infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of workers; when serious occupational disease hazards occur, they shall have the right to demand the adoption of protective measures, or suggest to the relevant government departments the adoption of compulsory measures; when an occupational disease hazard accident occurs, they shall have the right to participate in the investigation and handling of the accident; when they discover circumstances that endanger the life and health of workers, they shall have the right to suggest to the employing unit that workers be evacuated from the dangerous site, and the employing unit shall immediately deal with the matter.

Article 41 Expenses incurred by employing units for the prevention and control of occupational disease hazards, workplace health testing, health surveillance and occupational health training, as required for the prevention and treatment of occupational diseases, shall be actually listed in the production costs in accordance with the relevant state provisions.

Article 42 The occupational health supervision and administration departments shall, in accordance with their respective division of functions and duties, strengthen the supervision and inspection of the implementation of occupational disease protection management measures by employing units, exercise their powers according to law, and assume responsibility.

Article 44 A worker may undergo diagnosis of an occupational disease at a medical and health institution that undertakes the diagnosis of occupational diseases according to law in the place where the employing unit is located, the place of the worker's domicile, or the place of the worker's habitual residence.

Article 45 The diagnostic criteria for occupational diseases and the measures for the diagnosis and appraisal of occupational diseases shall be formulated by the health administration department of the State Council. The measures for the appraisal of the grade of disability caused by occupational diseases shall be formulated by the labor and social security administration department of the State Council jointly with the health administration department of the State Council.

Article 47 Employing units shall truthfully provide materials required for the diagnosis and appraisal of occupational diseases, such as the workers' occupational history, history of exposure to occupational disease hazards, and the test results of occupational disease hazard factors in the workplace; the health administration department shall supervise, inspect and urge the employing units to provide the aforesaid materials; workers and relevant institutions shall also provide materials related to the diagnosis and appraisal of occupational diseases.
When the diagnosis or appraisal institution for occupational diseases needs to know about the situation of occupational disease hazard factors in the workplace, it may conduct an onsite investigation of the workplace, or may request the health administration department to do so, and the health administration department shall organize an onsite investigation within ten days. The employing unit shall not refuse or obstruct.

Article 48 In the process of diagnosis and appraisal of occupational diseases, if the employing unit fails to provide such materials as the test results of occupational disease hazard factors in the workplace, the diagnosis or appraisal institution shall make its conclusion based on the worker's clinical manifestations, auxiliary examination results, occupational history and history of exposure to occupational disease hazards, and with reference to the worker's own statements and the daily supervision and inspection information provided by the health administration department.
If a worker has objections to the materials provided by the employing unit, such as the test results of occupational disease hazard factors in the workplace, or if there is no employing unit to provide the aforesaid materials due to the dissolution or bankruptcy of the worker's employing unit, the diagnosis or appraisal institution shall request the health administration department to conduct an investigation, and the health administration department shall, within thirty days of receiving the request, make a determination on the disputed materials or the situation of occupational disease hazard factors in the workplace; the relevant departments shall cooperate.

Article 49 In the process of diagnosis and appraisal of occupational diseases, when confirming a worker's occupational history and history of exposure to occupational disease hazards, if the parties dispute the labor relationship, type of work, job position, or period of employment, they may apply to the local labor and personnel dispute arbitration commission for arbitration; the labor and personnel dispute arbitration commission that receives the application shall accept it and render an award within thirty days.
During the arbitration process, the parties shall have the responsibility to provide evidence for the claims they assert. If a worker is unable to provide evidence in the possession or under the management of the employing unit that is relevant to the arbitration claim, the arbitration tribunal shall require the employing unit to provide it within a specified period; if the employing unit fails to provide it within the specified period, it shall bear adverse consequences.
If a worker is not satisfied with the arbitration award, he or she may file a lawsuit with the People's Court according to law.
If an employing unit is not satisfied with the arbitration award, it may file a lawsuit with the People's Court according to law within fifteen days from the date of conclusion of the occupational disease diagnosis or appraisal procedure; during the period of litigation, the worker's treatment costs shall be paid through the channels prescribed for the treatment of occupational diseases.

Article 50 When an employing unit or a medical and health institution discovers a patient with an occupational disease or a patient suspected of having an occupational disease, it shall promptly report to the local health administration department. If the disease is diagnosed as an occupational disease, the employing unit shall also report to the local labor and social security administration department. The department that receives the report shall handle the matter according to law.

Article 51 The health administrative department of the local people's government at or above the county level shall be responsible for the management of occupational disease statistical reports within its administrative region and shall report them to the higher authorities in accordance with the relevant provisions.

Article 52 Where a party has any objection to the diagnosis of an occupational disease, he may apply to the health administrative department of the local people's government at the place where the medical and health institution that made the diagnosis is located for an expert evaluation.
A dispute over the diagnosis of an occupational disease shall be subject to expert evaluation by an occupational disease diagnosis appraisal committee organized by the health administrative department of the local people's government at or above the city with districts level upon the application of the party.
Where a party is not satisfied with the appraisal conclusion made by the occupational disease diagnosis appraisal committee at the city with districts level, he may apply to the health administrative department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government for a re-appraisal.

Article 53 An occupational disease diagnosis appraisal committee shall be composed of experts in relevant specialties.
The health administrative department of the people's government of a province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government shall establish a relevant expert database. When it is necessary to make a diagnosis appraisal of an occupational disease dispute, the parties or the relevant health administrative department entrusted by the parties shall determine the experts to serve on the diagnosis appraisal committee by random selection from the expert database.
An occupational disease diagnosis appraisal committee shall make the diagnosis appraisal in accordance with the occupational disease diagnosis standards and the occupational disease diagnosis and appraisal measures promulgated by the health administrative department of the State Council, and shall issue a written certificate of occupational disease diagnosis appraisal to the parties. The expenses for occupational disease diagnosis and appraisal shall be borne by the employer.

Article 54 Members of an occupational disease diagnosis appraisal committee shall abide by professional ethics, conduct diagnosis appraisal objectively and impartially, and bear corresponding responsibilities. Members of an occupational disease diagnosis appraisal committee shall not contact the parties in private, shall not accept any property or other benefits from the parties, and shall withdraw if they have an interest in the parties.
Where a People's Court accepts a relevant case and an occupational disease appraisal is required, it shall select experts to participate in the appraisal from the relevant expert database lawfully established by the health administrative department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government.

Article 55 Where a medical and health institution finds a suspected occupational disease patient, it shall inform the worker himself and promptly notify the employer.
The employer shall promptly arrange for the diagnosis of the suspected occupational disease patient; during the period of diagnosis or medical observation of the suspected occupational disease patient, the employer shall not dissolve or terminate the labor contract concluded with him.
The expenses incurred by a suspected occupational disease patient during the period of diagnosis or medical observation shall be borne by the employer.

Article 56 The employer shall ensure that occupational disease patients enjoy the occupational disease benefits prescribed by the State according to law.
The employer shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, arrange for occupational disease patients to undergo treatment, rehabilitation and regular check-ups.
The employer shall transfer an occupational disease patient who is no longer fit to continue his original work from his original post and shall properly place him.
The employer shall grant appropriate job allowances to workers who are engaged in operations involving exposure to occupational disease hazards.

Article 57 The expenses for diagnosis, treatment and rehabilitation of occupational disease patients, and the social security for occupational disease patients who are disabled or have lost their capacity to work, shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State on work-related injury insurance.

Article 58 In addition to enjoying work-related injury insurance according to law, an occupational disease patient who still has the right to compensation under relevant civil laws shall have the right to claim compensation from the employer.

Article 59 Where a worker is diagnosed with an occupational disease, but the employer has not participated in work-related injury insurance according to law, the employer shall bear the worker's medical care and living expenses.

Article 60 Where an occupational disease patient changes his work unit, the benefits he enjoys according to law shall remain unchanged.
Where an employer undergoes division, merger, dissolution, bankruptcy or other circumstances, it shall conduct health examinations for workers engaged in operations involving exposure to occupational disease hazards, and shall properly place occupational disease patients in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

Article 61 An occupational disease patient whose employer no longer exists or whose labor relationship cannot be confirmed may apply to the local people's government's medical security or civil affairs departments for medical assistance and assistance in living and other aspects.
Local people's governments at all levels shall, in light of the actual conditions of their respective regions, take other measures to ensure that the occupational disease patients as mentioned in the preceding paragraph receive medical treatment.

Article 62 The occupational health supervision and administration departments of the people's governments at or above the county level shall, in accordance with the laws and regulations on the prevention and control of occupational diseases, national occupational health standards and hygiene requirements, and within the scope of their respective duties, conduct supervision and inspection over the work of prevention and control of occupational diseases.

Article 63 When performing the duty of supervision and inspection, the health administrative department shall have the power to take the following measures:
(1) entering the unit under inspection and the site of occupational disease hazards to learn about the situation and to investigate and collect evidence;
(2) consulting or copying materials related to acts violating the laws and regulations on the prevention and control of occupational diseases and collecting samples; and
(3) ordering the units and individuals that violate the laws and regulations on the prevention and control of occupational diseases to cease their illegal acts.

Article 64 Where an occupational disease hazard accident occurs or there is evidence proving that a hazardous condition may lead to an occupational disease hazard accident, the health administrative department may take the following temporary control measures:
(1) ordering the suspension of the operations causing the occupational disease hazard accident;
(2) sealing up the materials and equipment that have caused or may cause an occupational disease hazard accident; and
(3) organizing the control of the scene of the occupational disease hazard accident.
After the occupational disease hazard accident or hazardous condition has been effectively brought under control, the health administrative department shall promptly lift the control measures.

Article 65 When performing their duties according to law, occupational health supervision and law enforcement personnel shall produce their supervision law enforcement credentials.
Occupational health supervision and law enforcement personnel shall be devoted to their duties, enforce the law impartially, and strictly abide by law enforcement norms; where the secrets of employers are involved, they shall keep them confidential.

Article 66 When occupational health supervision and law enforcement personnel perform their duties according to law, the unit being inspected shall accept the inspection and provide support and cooperation, and shall not refuse or obstruct it.

Article 68 Occupational health supervision and law enforcement personnel shall undergo qualification accreditation according to law.
The occupational health supervision and administration departments shall strengthen team building, improve the political and professional quality of occupational health supervision and law enforcement personnel, establish and improve internal supervision systems in accordance with the provisions of this Law and other relevant laws and regulations, and conduct supervision and inspection over their staff members' implementation of laws and regulations and compliance with discipline.

Article 73 Where a person who provides equipment or materials that may generate occupational disease hazards to an employer fails to provide a Chinese instruction manual or set up warning signs and Chinese warning notices as required, the health administrative department shall order him to make corrections within a specified time limit, give him a warning, and concurrently impose a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan.

Article 74 Where an employer or a medical and health institution fails to report occupational diseases or suspected occupational diseases as required, the relevant competent department shall, within the scope of its duties, order it to make corrections within a specified time limit, give it a warning, and may concurrently impose a fine of not more than 10,000 yuan; if it practices fraud, a concurrent fine of not less than 20,000 yuan but not more than 50,000 yuan shall be imposed; and the directly responsible person in charge and other directly liable persons may be given a demotion or dismissal sanction according to law.

Article 76 Where a person produces, deals in or imports equipment or materials that may generate occupational disease hazards and are explicitly prohibited by the State, he shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations.

Article 77 Where an employer violates the provisions of this Law and has caused serious harm to the life and health of workers, the health administrative department shall order it to suspend operations that cause occupational disease hazards, or request the relevant people's government to order its closure within the limits of authority prescribed by the State Council, and concurrently impose a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan.

Article 78 Where an employer violates the provisions of this Law, causing a major occupational disease hazard accident or other serious consequences, which constitutes a crime, the directly responsible person in charge and other directly liable persons shall be investigated for criminal liability according to law.

Article 79 Where a person engages in occupational health technical services without obtaining the qualification accreditation for such services, the health administrative department shall order him to immediately cease the illegal act and confiscate the illegal gains; if the illegal gains are more than 5,000 yuan, a concurrent fine of not less than two times but not more than ten times the illegal gains shall be imposed; if there are no illegal gains or the illegal gains are less than 5,000 yuan, a concurrent fine of not less than 5,000 yuan but not more than 50,000 yuan shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, the directly responsible person in charge and other directly liable persons shall be given a demotion, dismissal or expulsion sanction according to law.

Article 80 Where an institution engaged in occupational health technical services or a medical and health institution undertaking the diagnosis of occupational diseases violates the provisions of this Law and commits any of the following acts, the health administrative department shall order it to immediately cease the illegal act, give it a warning, and confiscate the illegal gains; if the illegal gains are more than 5,000 yuan, a concurrent fine of not less than two times but not more than five times the illegal gains shall be imposed; if there are no illegal gains or the illegal gains are less than 5,000 yuan, a concurrent fine of not less than 5,000 yuan but not more than 20,000 yuan shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, the original accreditation or registration authority shall revoke its corresponding qualification; the directly responsible person in charge and other directly liable persons shall be given a demotion, dismissal or expulsion sanction according to law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law:
(1) engaging in occupational health technical services or occupational disease diagnosis beyond the scope of the qualification accreditation or the registered diagnosis and treatment items;
(2) failing to perform statutory duties in accordance with the provisions of this Law; or
(3) issuing false certification documents.

Article 81 Where a member of an occupational disease diagnosis appraisal committee accepts property or other benefits from a party to an occupational disease diagnosis dispute, he shall be given a warning, his accepted property shall be confiscated, and he may be concurrently fined not less than 3,000 yuan but not more than 50,000 yuan; his qualification as a member of the occupational disease diagnosis appraisal committee shall be revoked, and he shall be removed from the expert database established by the health administrative department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government.

Article 82 Where a health administrative department fails to report occupational diseases and occupational disease hazard accidents in accordance with the relevant provisions, the administrative department at the next higher level shall order it to make corrections, circulate a notice of criticism, and give it a warning; where it makes false reports or conceals the facts, the person in charge of the unit, the directly responsible person in charge and other directly liable persons shall be given a demotion, dismissal or expulsion sanction according to law.

Article 83 Where a local people's government at or above the county level fails to perform its duties in accordance with this Law in the work of prevention and control of occupational diseases, and a major occupational disease hazard accident occurs within its administrative region, causing serious social impact, the directly responsible person in charge and other directly liable persons shall be given a sanction ranging from a major demerit to expulsion according to law.
Where the occupational health supervision and administration department of a people's government at or above the county level fails to perform its duties as provided for in this Law, abuses its power, neglects its duties, or engages in illegal practices for personal gain, the directly responsible person in charge and other directly liable persons shall be given a sanction of a major demerit or demotion according to law; where an occupational disease hazard accident or other serious consequences are caused, they shall be given a sanction of dismissal or expulsion according to law.
Article 84 Where a violation of the provisions of this Law constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 85 For the purpose of this Law, the following terms have the meanings ascribed to them hereunder:
"Occupational disease hazards" refers to various hazards that may cause occupational diseases to workers engaged in occupational activities. "Occupational disease hazard factors" include various harmful chemical, physical and biological factors existing in occupational activities as well as other occupational harmful factors generated during the working process.
"Occupational contraindications" refers to a special physiological or pathological state of a worker who, when engaged in a specific occupation or exposed to specific occupational disease hazard factors, is more susceptible to occupational disease hazards and occupational diseases than the general occupational population, or which may cause aggravation of his original disease, or which may induce a disease that may endanger the life and health of others during the working process.

Article 86 Where a unit other than an employer as prescribed in Article 2 of this Law generates occupational disease hazards, its activities for the prevention and control of occupational diseases may be implemented by reference to this Law.
The entity that uses dispatched workers shall fulfill the obligations of an employer as provided for in this Law.
The measures for the People's Liberation Army to implement this Law by reference shall be formulated by the State Council and the Central Military Commission.

Article 87 The supervision and administration of the control of radioactive occupational disease hazards in medical institutions shall be implemented by the health administrative department in accordance with the provisions of this Law.
Article 88 This Law shall come into force as of May 1, 2002.
